stem: A video production company runs two workloads: dozens of render nodes that all read and write many small files on one shared file system at once, and a nightly batch job that streams a large sequential dataset from a single attached volume. Which TWO configurations meet these performance needs? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Amazon EFS with General Purpose performance mode and Provisioned throughput
Amazon EFS with Max I/O performance mode and Elastic throughput
An sc1 Cold HDD volume for the nightly job
An st1 Throughput Optimized HDD volume for the nightly job
A gp3 general purpose SSD volume for the nightly job

rationale: Max I/O trades a little per-operation latency for higher aggregate throughput and IOPS across a very large number of concurrently connected clients doing small parallel operations, which matches the render-node pattern, and Elastic throughput scales bandwidth automatically as demand grows. st1's baseline and burst throughput profile is built for large sequential workloads accessed frequently, matching a nightly streaming batch job. General Purpose performance mode gives the lowest latency for a single client's operations, not the best fit for dozens of nodes doing many small parallel operations at once, and Provisioned throughput is meant for a small, hot file system rather than this many concurrent clients. gp3 is an SSD priced and tuned for IOPS-oriented random access, not the throughput-priced profile a large sequential streaming job needs. sc1 is priced for infrequently accessed data at a lower baseline throughput than st1, not a job that streams data every night.
